Export controls on advanced chips are tightening after U.S. officials moved to close loopholes that let Chinese firms tap Nvidia's computing power. When rules shift this hard, capital often looks for leaders with real skin in the game. Founder led businesses with high insider ownership and solid balance sheets can be one way to lean into that. This article walks through three such stocks from our curated screener.

The three founder led businesses covered below are only a sample, with the full screen surfacing 26 more companies where insiders hold meaningful stakes and balance sheets look equally resilient. To size up that wider field quickly, head straight into the Top Founder-Led Companies screener to identify, analyze, and prioritize the founder led setups that best match your own conviction profile.

Vicor (VICR)

Vicor is a founder led power electronics specialist, where high insider ownership and long serving management back a focused modular power systems franchise. The analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St frames that commitment through an AI ready roadmap, licensing income, and large scale manufacturing plans.

Vicor designs and manufactures modular power components and custom power systems, with all reported business revenue of about US$561 million coming from advanced or brick format products. The stock carries a market value of roughly US$7.34b.

"The ongoing transition to electric vehicles, particularly higher voltage architectures that require efficient conversion to 48V, remains ahead of Vicor. The broader focus on high density power modules across transportation and industrial customers positions future design wins to feed into revenue and earnings."

What happens if one quiet assumption in that roadmap shifts, and it shows up not in demand, but in future margin quality?

That margin question is exactly where the full narrative for Vicor digs in, mapping how Vicor's roadmap could turn today's assumptions into accelerating operating leverage or expose overlooked pressure points.

Today's Featured Research Reports

Taiwan Semiconductor's shares were in line with the Zacks Semiconductor - Circuit Foundry industry over the year-to-date period (+32% vs. +32%). The company benefits from rising demand for AI computing and a process roadmap that brings customers to successive technology generations. Its design ecosystem and advanced packaging services deepen customer relationships, while manufacturing scale and cash generation support continued investment. 

Overseas capacity adds geographic choice for customers but carries lasting cost disadvantages. Heavy capital commitments and recurring new-process ramp costs can limit how much revenue growth converts into shareholder cash returns. 

Customer concentration, supply bottlenecks and uneven consumer demand also constrain the breadth of growth. Currency exposure, export licensing, and a production base concentrated in Taiwan leave earnings sensitive to factors beyond chip adoption, even as productivity efforts partially offset them.

(You can read the full research report on Taiwan Semiconductor here >>>)

Shares of Johnson & Johnson have outperformed the Zacks Large Cap Pharmaceuticals industry over the year-to-date period (+40.3% vs. +29.1%). The company's Innovative Medicines unit is its primary growth engine despite Stelara LOE, driven by key products like Darzalex, Tremfya and Erleada and new drugs, Spravato, Carvykti and Tecvayli. J&J has also rapidly advanced its pipeline in the past year that will help drive growth through the back half of the decade. 

The company has "line of sight" to double-digit top-line growth by the end of the decade. However, J&J's MedTech growth remains constrained by weaker Abiomed demand, China's volume-based procurement and electrophysiology competition. 

J&J also faces pressure from Stelara's LOE and rising generic/biosimilar competition across several drugs. The talc litigation also remains a financial overhang, with the proposed settlement still conditional.

(You can read the full research report on Johnson & Johnson here >>>)

Palantir's shares have underperformed the Zacks Internet - Software industry over the year-to-date period (-5.5% vs. -2%). The company is facing intense competition from larger rivals, rising technical expenses and fixed cloud commitments could pressure margins and constrain cost flexibility. Concentrated receivables pose cash flow risks, while the absence of dividends limits its appeal to income-focused investors. 

These risks temper growth prospects, supporting a Neutral recommendation on PLTR. Nevertheless, PLTR's share pieces reflecting optimism surrounding its AI-driven growth prospects. 

Rising adoption of its AI platforms across government and commercial markets, expanding customer relationships and strong cash generation support sustained growth. Its land-and-expand strategy and ample liquidity provide flexibility to fund innovation, product development and technical hiring. 

(You can read the full research report on Palantir here >>>)

Shares of Investors Title have gained +4.5% over the year-to-date period against the Zacks Insurance - Property and Casualty industry's gain of +16.3%. This microcap company with a market capitalization of $480.47 million sees its premium growth supported by higher real estate transaction volumes, geographic expansion and favorable net title insurance rate changes. Third-quarter 2026 net premiums written rose 20.9%, while its sizable investment portfolio and sound liquidity provide resilience. 

The board also declared a $19.27-per-share special dividend alongside its regular quarterly payout. However, claims provisions and agent commissions rose sharply, contributing to a decline in third-quarter earnings and margins. 

Weakness in like-kind exchange activity limits diversification, and the title business remains sensitive to housing conditions and concentrated regional markets. These offsetting factors temper the outlook despite continued premium momentum, substantial capital resources and long-term expansion opportunities.

(You can read the full research report on Investors Title here >>>)

Altigen Communications' shares have gained +1% over the year-to-date period against the Zacks Communication - Components industry's gain of +38.1%. This microcap company with a market capitalization of $11.13 million, has seen its cloud transition gaining momentum as new cloud revenues have begun exceeding legacy churn, supported by its largest-ever cloud customer, larger enterprise wins and an expanding AI portfolio. 

CoreInteract, CoreEngage and CoreInsights broaden its addressable market and create cross-selling opportunities, while the Fiserv relationship offers a scalable channel into financial services. Its installed MAXCloud and MaxCS base also provides a lower-friction path for cloud migrations and AI adoption. 

However, the company's fiscal third-quarter revenues fell 14.2%, margins compressed, and customer concentration remained high at 74% for the top five customers and resellers. Rising development spending and impairment risk add uncertainty. At 0.61X EV/sales, valuation remains below industry levels and historical medians. 

(You can read the full research report on Altigen Communications here >>>)

Partnership kicks off with a November 19 webinar and brings Silvia's users education on income strategies beyond traditional fixed income

NEW YORK, Nov. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Direxion, a leading provider of specialized ETFs with approximately $70.8 billion in assets under management (as of September 30, 2026), today announced a partnership with Silvia, Inc. (Nasdaq: SVIA), the first publicly traded agentic finance firm.

Direxion

Through the partnership, Direxion will provide Silvia's users with webinars, content and other resources on pursuing income beyond traditional fixed income strategies, including options-based approaches such as Direxion's Defined Income Boost ETFs, which seek to generate income from stocks many investors already follow: NVIDIA, Tesla, Alphabet, Meta, Palantir and Micron.

"Investors make better decisions when they are well informed, especially on something as important as generating income. We're pleased to partner with Anthony, who clearly shares our passion for education, as illustrated by his mission to build the Silvia platform, which is designed to help investors feel more confident and prepared as they plan for the income they need," said Douglas Yones, Chief Executive Officer at Direxion.

The partnership will launch with an inaugural webinar for Silvia's users on Thursday, November 19, at 2 p.m. ET, featuring a conversation between Anthony Pompliano, Chairman and CEO of Silvia, Inc., and Bilal Little, Global ETF Strategist at Direxion. The partnership will continue into 2027 with additional collaborations in the works.

Silvia was co-founded by Anthony Pompliano, an entrepreneur, investor and best-selling author. "Our mission is to help independent investors make money," said Mr. Pompliano. "Partnering with Direxion on educational content gives our users access to clear, practical information about strategies they may want to evaluate as part of their broader financial picture."

Direxion is best known for its leadership in leveraged and inverse ETFs, particularly in technology, with funds such as the Direxion Daily Semiconductor Bull & Bear 3X Shares (SOXL/SOXS), among the most actively traded ETFs globally*, the Direxion Daily TSLA Bull 2X and Bear 1X Shares (TSLL/TSLS), and the Direxion Daily SpaceX Bull & Bear 2X ETFs (LOFF/LOFD). The firm recently announced plans to launch the Direxion Daily Anthropic Bull & Bear 2X ETFs (ANTO/ANTD), expected to begin trading on the first trading day after Anthropic's IPO.

Why Does Palantir Stock Keep Going Down?
Rich Smith, The Motley Fool

NVDA

Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Palantir Technologies (NASDAQ:PLTR) stock dropped another 3.7% through 2 p.m. ET Monday, its third straight trading day of losses. And why?

"Because... Nvidia," I suppose?

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Image source: The Motley Fool.

Everything's Nvidia these days

In case you haven't heard, multiple stories emerged alleging affairs by Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang last week, leading to the CEO's resignation -- and panicking AI investors. No one's entirely certain why, with theories ranging from potential tightening of U.S. regulation on semiconductor exports to worries Nvidia will have to stop financing its own customers' chip purchases to simple fear that "Jensen Huang is magic," and without his presence, this whole AI revolution thing will fall apart.

And maybe that's true; I just don't know that it has much to do with Palantir.

Is Palantir an AI company? Sure. But it doesn't do much business with China (close to 0%, according to data from S&P Global Market Intelligence). Nor have I heard anything about Palantir subsidizing purchases of its own products, as Nvidia does. To me, this seems more like a case of investors knee-jerk selling anything related to AI.

What's next for Palantir

Meanwhile, Palantir just won a better price target from Phillip Securities analyst Alif Fahmi this morning. Fahmi points out that Palantir has grown its revenue 92% so far this year, and will hold onto most of that growth -- 91% -- through year-end. Rating the stock a "buy," the analyst is raising his price target to $248 per share.

Is Fahmi right? Could Palantir stock gain 54% in the next 12 months? I don't know about that. But at 99x free cash flow and a projected earnings growth rate of 62.5% over the next five years, Palantir is nonetheless approaching my own buy-it-now price.

A little lower, and I might just buy Palantir stock myself.

Palantir Technologies (NASDAQ:PLTR) primarily generates revenue by engineering highly sophisticated software systems that facilitate complex data integration, secure data management, and advanced analytics for national intelligence agencies, defense organizations, and large commercial enterprises globally, helping them manage unstructured data.

It secured a major production agreement from the U.S. Army to manufacture advanced intelligence targeting ground stations, and it simultaneously established fresh collaborations with Nebius Group and Nvidia to enhance the commercial delivery of its software models.

Why Revenue Matters for Investors

Revenue serves as a primary financial baseline for individual investors to evaluate because it establishes the total amount of incoming money a business generates from its daily operations before accounting for payroll, taxes, or general operating expenses. Tracking this metric reveals whether an organization is successfully attracting customers and growing its overall business volume over time.
